summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (61/46)

data.turoyo: Hawi fəlge d lalyo, ḥəlle aṯi taʕlo, mxapalle ʕal u qawro du babo.
data.translation: Es wurde Mitternacht, da sah er, wie ein Fuchs kam und auf dem Grabe des Vaters herumscharrte.

rationale: First attested Preterit box, matching inherited mxapalle base; ʕal marks the grave being scratched at.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/47)

data.turoyo: Gdoṯe, gdoṯe, kul+naqla gəmxapər, gəmxapər, doxele. <...>
data.translation: It would come, it would come, every time it digs, it digs to eat him.
data.ref: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/47

rationale: Thin Infectum 1; repeated x-p-r form gives a source-faithful contrast with inherited x-r-p spelling.

evidence.cite: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/47

summary: All four tokens fit II.1 aufgraben, aufkratzen. Preterit mxapalle supplies a missing box, while repeated gəmxapər marks recurrent digging with kul+naqla.

The greyhound and fox uses have no overt material object; the grave is ʕal-marked. The inherited ostrich construction has b-ground and b-foot instrument. These do not establish another sense or a Detransitive.

The entry’s ostrich form gəmxarpo reverses the final root consonants relative to mxapər. This is actual source spelling in 81/116; preserve it and do not turn it into a new xrp root or silently repair it.
Is mxarpo versus mxapər a dialectal alternation, metathesis in performance, or a transcription error? The supplied evidence cannot decide.
Remove the extra it before eat.
rationale: The translation accidentally repeats it across the verb: does not it eat it. The Turoyo lo=k-uxlo-le and the corpus translation frißt er es nicht express does not eat it.
and is accidentally repeated in the English translation.
